v.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes Adam toward divergence (e.g. experiments 67 and 66 showed big drops).
Very small learning rates leave the network undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing them helps (experiments 61 and 68).
Stepping down from an unstable high learning rate restores stable training (experiments 74 and 75).
Lowering an already small learning rate leaves the model more undertrained (experiments 77 and 78).
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty causes underfitting (experiment 7).
Relaxing an overly strong L2 penalty reduces underfitting (experiments 13, 14 and 19).
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding units helps more than when the network is already wide.
Deeper ReLU networks trained with a large learning rate are more prone to unstable training (experiment 50).
Removing a layer stabilizes training when the learning rate is large (experiments 55 and 60).
With fixed epochs, very large batches mean few updates, so going larger undertrains the model further.
